solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Only fair

blocks.note: the adverb, as in 'only a minute'
the adjective, as in a fair ruling

explanation.walkthrough: Two words side by side, each a different sense of the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plain synonyms: just as an adverb means only (just two left), and as an adjective means fair (a just verdict).

clue.text: Charlie, a contract killer missing his last shots, exhausted

indicators.note: the killer loses his final letter
SHOTS emptied of its middle leaves only its outside letters

blocks.clueFragment: a contract killer missing his last
blocks.note: JACKAL, the assassin of The Day of the Jackal, without his last letter L

explanation.surface: A hitman called Charlie has fired off all his ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: A charlie is British slang for a fool, as is a jackass; the surface makes Charlie a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is British slang for a fool, a regional use that a jackass, a plain word for an idiot, matches.

clue.text: Next generation Colt a bit of a rascal?

blocks.note: the next generation is a SON, and a Colt is a make OF A GUN
a mild name for a rogue

explanation.surface: A young horse from the next generation shows early signs of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt reads as a young horse, which suits 'next generation'; here it is the revolver maker, so the offspring of a Colt is a son of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: 'You son of a gun!' is said of a likeable rascal.

clue.text: Special tool for cutting small tree, if Ken is bothered

indicators.note: letters that are bothered are stirred up and rearranged

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man named Ken is worried about which tool to use on a small tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool for cutting small tree' reads like a saw; the definition stops at 'cutting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak knife is a serrated knife made specially for cutting meat.

clue.text: Laugh almost about tense work to cut ivory

indicators.note: the laugh stops one letter short
the laugh goes around the T

explanation.surface: Someone stifles a laugh while working under pressure on a piece of ivory.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivory stands for teeth, so to teethe is to work at cutting ivory, as a baby does.
explanation.definitionFit: A teething baby is working to cut its first teeth, and teeth are ivories.

clue.text: Taking on commercial financial derivative

blocks.note: a TV commercial is an ad
an option is a derivative contract

explanation.surface: A firm is taking on a commercial financial product.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking on reads as hiring or confronting; here it is the noun for taking something up, as a child or a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the taking on of a child, an idea or a policy.

clue.text: Order, order at length irks PM

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them

explanation.surface: The Speaker's repeated cries of 'Order, order!' go on so long that the Prime Minister gets annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first 'Order' is the definition (a religious order), the second tells you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knights Templar were a medieval military religious order.

clue.text: Moon landing had upset state

indicators.note: the other letters land inside the moon
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

blocks.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A moon landing had disturbed the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the Apollo landing unsettling a country; 'landing' says the upset HAD lands inside the moon IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Idaho is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Alternative to paper for those trying to make plane?

definitions.text: Alternative to paper for those trying to make plane?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a material other than paper for folding

blocks.clueFragment: for those trying to make plane?
blocks.note: meant: travellers trying to catch a flight, who need a paperless ticket

explanation.surface: Someone building a paper plane looks for a different material.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests making a model aircraft out of something other than paper; 'make' means catch, as in making a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-ticket is the paperless ticket air travellers use to catch a plane.

clue.text: Phone card Kerry lost somewhere on the Tube

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered out of order

explanation.surface: A woman called Kerry mislaid her phone card on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, and Hyde Park Corner is one of its stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a station on the Piccadilly line of the London Underground.

clue.text: Sir Arthur missing a new and an old ball?

indicators.note: the name goes without the listed letters

blocks.note: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes

explanation.surface: Sir Arthur has gone without a new ball and an old one.
explanation.walkthrough: CONAN DOYLE without A, N and O leaves CONDYLE; 'ball' is anatomical, not a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A condyle is the rounded knob at the end of a bone that forms a joint.

clue.text: Work with paper in Tokyo, Riga, Miami

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A paper-related job is available in three world cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Tokyo is a nod to Japan, the home of origami.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper.

clue.text: Animated Child Catcher of UK’s ultimate auteur

indicators.note: animated letters are brought to life and moved
ultimate means last, so UK's ultimate is its final letter

explanation.surface: The Child Catcher, the villain of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, as created by Britain's supreme film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Child Catcher is the sinister villain of the film Chitty Chitty Bang Bang, which suits a master of suspense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock is the classic example of an auteur, a director whose films bear a personal stamp.

clue.text: Remarkable message

blocks.note: the adjective, as in a notable achievement
the noun, something sent to convey information

explanation.surface: Someone praises an extraordinary note.
explanation.walkthrough: Remarkable looks like praise for the message; they are two separate senses, one adjective and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means notable; as a noun it is a message sent.

clue.text: Show respect, then show disrespect when receiving king in Spar

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the spitting word takes the king inside it

blocks.note: bow as a mark of respect

explanation.surface: Someone bows to the king, then turns rude, perhaps at a sparring match.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar reads as box or argue; here it is a ship's pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is the spar projecting forward from a ship's bow.

clue.text: Fed up with this chatter, a constant for those attending

indicators.note: as heard by an audience, so a sound-alike

blocks.note: British slang: to rabbit on is to chatter
the constant pi, heard as pie

explanation.surface: Someone is sick of all this constant chatter directed at the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up with' means served up as food, not bored; 'constant' is the mathematical pi.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a pun: 'fed up with this' means served this to eat, and rabbit pie is one such dish.

clue.text: With which to reach Spooner’s distant county?

indicators.note: swap the opening sounds of the two words

blocks.note: far = distant; its F sound is swapped for the county's K sound
Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland; its K sound is swapped for F

explanation.surface: A question about how to get to a far-off county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Kerry is in the south-west of Ireland, and the car ferry is one way to get there from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A car ferry is a vessel with which you reach places across water.

clue.text: Solo quietly leaving excellent hotel celebration

indicators.note: quietly is P, and leaving means that P walks out of the word for excellent

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lone guest slips quietly out of a party at a first-class hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Solo is Han Solo, not alone; pukka is British slang for genuine or first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanukkah is the Jewish festival of lights.

clue.text: Journalist witnessed item smuggled into gaol?

explanation.surface: A reporter saw something being smuggled into prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: the hacksaw hidden in a cake is a jailbreak cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is the classic tool smuggled to prisoners for sawing through bars.

clue.text: After exercise bubblier, regularly lost a stone

indicators.note: PE comes first, the rest after it
every other letter is dropped

explanation.surface: After a workout on fizzier drinks, someone shed some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is also a British unit of weight (14 lb), which the surface uses for losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a pebble is a small smooth stone worn round by water.

clue.text: Land reportedly more rocky beneath earth

indicators.note: as spoken, so a sound-alike
in a down clue, it goes below E

explanation.surface: Farmland is said to be rockier under the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth is E in electrical wiring; in a down entry 'beneath' puts the sound-alike under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Estonia is a Baltic land, one of many countries.

clue.text: Mafia family boss killing over hat

indicators.note: to kill is to remove, so killing over takes the O (over, in cricket) out of the boss

blocks.note: CAPO, a Mafia boss, without O (over, in cricket)

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss orders a hit over a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A capo is a Mafia boss; the surface reads as a gangland hit, but the killing is only of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobcap is a soft round indoor bonnet worn in the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: Copy FT and publish extent of emissions

blocks.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: An instruction to copy an article in the Financial Times and publish it.
explanation.walkthrough: FT looks like the Financial Times newspaper, but it expands to the unit it abbreviates.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon footprint measures the greenhouse gas emissions caused by a person or activity.

clue.text: Relax with joint cycling

indicators.note: the last letters move round to the front

blocks.note: a mitre joint, as in a picture frame

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a spliff while out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests a spliff or a knee; here it is the woodworker's mitre.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to relax or ease off, as in remitting a penalty or effort.

clue.text: Back in Tehran, I’m escaping group meeting

indicators.note: read the hidden letters backwards
the letters sit in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Back in Iran, someone is fleeing a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'in' together mean the letters are hidden in the clue and read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a seminar is a meeting of a class or group for discussion.

clue.text: Boots might have this pain ointment initially by November

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of ointment is used

blocks.note: a cramp is a muscular pain
N = November in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Boots, the British chemist chain, might stock a pain ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a British high-street pharmacy, which makes pain ointment look like the answer; the boots are climbing boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Crampons are spiked plates fitted to climbing boots for ice.

clue.text: Women’s drunken hen party crashed by maiden Daphne?

indicators.note: drunken letters are jumbled
M crashes into the anagrammed letters

blocks.note: W = women, as in WI (Women's Institute)
M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

explanation.surface: A rowdy hen party (a bride's night out with her friends) is gatecrashed by a young woman called Daphne.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Daphne was a naiad, a river nymph, who was turned into a laurel; the question mark marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne was a naiad, a water nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Star last to depart Sin City

indicators.note: depart means leave, so the last letter departs from the word

blocks.note: nickname of the Nevada gambling city; its second word is needed

explanation.surface: A celebrity is the last to leave Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: Sin City is Las Vegas; take the second word and drop its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.
